basis: Defining skeletal and corneal dysplasia; patent ductus arteriosus in 2/2. Developmental delay frequency unknown; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Childhood interstitial lung disease; extrapulmonary features of individual subtypes do not apply across this umbrella.
Hereditary peripheral neuropathy; optic atrophy and visual impairment each in 3/6. Distal amyotrophy and pes cavus each only 1/6.
Malignant gliomas arise in the central nervous system.
Congenital failure of neural tube closure affects brain or spinal cord; additional organ damage varies across subtypes.
Inflammation or degeneration of peripheral sensory nerves; no specific infectious or immune mechanism is established.
Immune-mediated inflammatory demyelination of the central nervous system, within the multiple sclerosis spectrum.
Central corneal ulceration; location alone does not establish an infectious or autoimmune cause.
Inherited macular retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy with reduced visual acuity; no established extraocular disease.
Mitochondrial myopathy with ophthalmoplegia and ptosis; conduction disease and ventricular bigeminy in 1/1 reported patient. Neurologic and hepatic findings only 5-29%.
Turner phenotype with gonadal dysgenesis; congenital cardiovascular defects occur in ~30-50% and renal malformations in ~30-40%. Short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Warburg micro syndrome is defined by severe neurodevelopmental disease, congenital ocular abnormalities including cataracts, and hypogonadism.
Defining limb/mandibular defects, cleft palate and missing teeth; airway obstruction in 30-79% and global developmental delay in 11/25 support pulmonary and neurologic involvement.
Inherited lipid disorder; atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed consequence. Tendon xanthomas do not establish functional tendon damage.
Infiltrating astrocytic neoplasm originates in the central nervous system.

Fibrosing renal tubular disease with kidney failure; pulmonary infiltrates in 2/2 and bronchiectasis in 1/2 support direct pulmonary involvement. Recurrent infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Bile duct paucity, heart defects and butterfly vertebrae are defining features; renal malformations/dysfunction occur in roughly 40% or more. Posterior embryotoxon is non-damaging.
Familial cortical myoclonus and epilepsy; tremor and myoclonus occur in 13/13 and seizures in 7/13.
Defining developmental brain disease; gingival overgrowth and scoliosis each occur in 30-79%. Visual dysfunction is mainly central; optic atrophy and ocular abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Defined by abnormal vertebral closure and spinal neural tissue involvement. Bladder dysfunction is not established in most patients across open and occult forms.
Cobalamin metabolic defect defined by megaloblastic anemia and encephalopathy; retinopathy occurs in 30-79%. Renal hemolytic-uremic syndrome occurs in only 1-4%.
Defining leukoencephalopathy and palmoplantar keratoderma; diaphyseal dysplasia occurs in 30-79%. Weakness reflects neurologic disease rather than primary muscle damage.
Pentose phosphate enzyme deficiency causing chronic erythrocyte hemolysis; splenomegaly belongs to the blood axis. Hemolytic jaundice does not establish liver damage.
Defining cutis laxa; emphysema and bronchiectasis each in 2/3. Cardiac defects/heart failure in 1/3 and pulmonary artery stenosis in 1/1 support cardiovascular involvement; samples are small.
Hereditary photodermatosis with photosensitivity, freckling and dry skin; no established common extracutaneous organ damage.
